lens: sceptic-stat: statistical validity. I re-estimated every claim from the data files with fresh code, using common.py only for loading and alignment. HAC is gap-aware and matches C.nw_ols to 1e-13 on contiguous samples. Other tools: AR(2) placebo calibration matched to each feature's persistence, circular-shift nulls of the target, moving-block bootstrap (block 8; block 4 for n=17), and HAC(4) vs HAC(8). Sensitivity samples drop 2021Q3-23Q4, COVID 2020-21, definition-break quarters (first 4 quarters of each new definition plus 2007Q2-Q4) and the 'echo' quarters 2022Q4-25Q3. I also compared WLS with OLS for og, ran BY/Holm/Bonferroni over the families as they were actually searched, and ran an expanding-window OOS test from 2010 (COVID quarters excluded from training) with Clark-West and Diebold-Mariano tests.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Same-quarter EU packaging and plastics PPI inflation is the strongest coincident correlate of d_margin, with a stable coefficient of -0.13 to -0.18pp per 1pp in every subsample. Its significance comes mostly from 2021Q3-23Q4 (70% of the covariance): HAC t is -9.6, but the block-bootstrap t is only -4.8. Without the episode t is -3.0 (placebo p=0.02, circular-shift p=0.08); before 2020 it is -1.9, and without the episode it fails BY among 200 features. For raw materials the trough is -0.67pp per +10% (lag 3, full) and -0.35pp without the episode, the latter not significant (t -1.7). The 6-7 quarter recovery appears only in that insignificant estimate without the episode.
verdicts.evidence: Packaging, coincident: b=-0.151, t=-9.6 (HAC4) / -11.0 (HAC8). Placebo 95% |t| is 2.74 (nominal size 17%), p<0.001. Circular shift p=0.011 (the floor). Block bootstrap: t=-4.8, CI [-0.23,-0.09]. Subsamples: without the episode -0.177, t -3.0 (HAC8 -3.1; bootstrap t -2.8); without COVID -0.137 (t -7.4); without breaks -0.132 (-6.5); without episode+COVID -0.146 (-2.5); before 2020 -0.134 (-1.9). Plastics at real-time h0: -0.174 (t -8.8), without the episode -0.196 (t -3.0), before 2020 t -2.1. Family check at real-time h0: plastics rank 1 of about 195 (calibrated Holm p<1e-5), packaging rank 4 (Holm 0.011). Without the episode, packaging is rank 11 (p_cal 0.017) and plastics rank 17 (p_cal 0.023), with BY=1.0; no core feature survives BY, and the top one is SE real-wage acceleration. Raw materials, K12 cubic PDL: full trough -0.67 at lag 3 (t -3.8; bootstrap 90% CI -1.08 to -0.22), no half recovery within 12 quarters (56% of bootstrap draws never recover). Without the episode: -0.35 at lag 2 (t -1.66), half recovery at lag 5 (90% CI 3-10), back to zero at lag 7. The trough lag depends on the specification: unrestricted K6 puts it at lag 0 (-1.16pp). FAO alone, without the episode: -0.14 (t -0.9).
verdicts.residual_doubt: Without the episode the evidence comes from very few cost cycles (2007-08 and 2011-12). Spot PPI and commodity series attenuate Orkla's true contract cost, so the size may be understated even as the significance is overstated.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Cost increases lower margins within 1-2 quarters: about -1.07pp per +10pp in the full sample (t -6.4) and -0.8pp without the episode (t -2.9). The response to decreases is not statistically different from zero (+0.4pp by lag 6 full, t 0.55; +1.05pp without the episode, t 1.4). Symmetry is rejected only in the full sample at lag 2, at the honest threshold (t -2.8 to -3.1), and not without the episode (t -1.4 to -1.9). Asymmetry is therefore suggestive, not established.
verdicts.evidence: raw_mat_wloc_yoy split into increases and decreases, lags 0-6, n=96; 43 quarters have negative inflation, so decreases are not rare. Quadratic PDL, HAC4: +10pp gives -1.06pp at lag 1 and -1.07pp at lag 2 (t -6.4); -10pp gives -0.42pp at lag 2, -0.23pp at lag 3 and +0.41pp at lag 6 (t 0.55). t for the cumulative difference: lag 2 -2.82 (HAC8 -3.07), lag 6 -0.31. Without the episode: increases -0.78pp at lag 2 (t -2.9); decreases +1.05pp at lag 6 (t 1.42; HAC8 1.58); difference t at lag 2 -1.85, at lag 6 +1.48. Unrestricted lags: difference at lag 2 -2.39 full and -1.45 without the episode. Without episode+echo: difference at lag 2 -1.41.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The point estimates do look asymmetric, and power is low with about 2 cycles of falling costs, so asymmetry may still be real.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Cost and price inflation 5-7 quarters back correlates positively with d_margin in sample (EU dairy PPI k=6: +0.068pp per 1pp, t 5.2). This mirrors the transitory margin hit, and it is not a usable leading signal. Placebo-calibrated BY over the d_margin lag family gives q=0.24 (Bonferroni over 8,400 tests gives 1), and the circular-shift p is 0.02-0.06. The lens's check without 2021Q3-23Q4 is contaminated by echo quarters, which supply 42% of the covariance. Adding lag-5-7 cost inflation to the AR does not improve forecasts from 2010: RMSE ratios are 0.98-1.09, and 1.01-1.03 when the lag-5-7 feature is chosen in real time.
verdicts.evidence: I reproduced the nominal result (t 5.16; BY within the target 0.004). Placebo 95% |t| is 2.67, so p_cal=2e-4. Calibrated BY is 0.24 within the 1,400-test d_margin family and 0.12 across 8,400 (padded with p=1); Bonferroni is 1. No positive-sign k>=4 d_margin row passes calibrated BY<0.10. Circular-shift p: dairy 0.045, SE food PPI 0.023, bakery 0.057, SE CPI 0.045 (two-sided). Echo: 2022Q4-25Q3 carries 42% of cov(d_margin, dairy k=6), and 2024Q2-Q3 alone 29%. t-stats full -> without episode -> without episode+echo -> also without 2007-09: dairy 5.16 / 5.53 / 3.36 / 2.82; SE food PPI 4.77 / 4.72 / 2.81 / 2.29; bakery k=5 4.47 / 5.52 / 3.35 / 2.30; SE CPI 4.18 / 4.32 / 2.72 / 2.08; weighted food PPI 3.78 / 3.72 / 1.17 / 0.23; packaging 2.96 / 3.74 / 1.41 / 1.00. Block-bootstrap t (full): dairy 3.7, bakery 2.0, SE CPI 1.6. OOS (AR plus the mean of cost-inflation lags 5-7, h=0/1/2/4, eval 2010-26): dairy 0.98-1.00, SE food PPI 0.997-1.008, bakery 1.02-1.04, SE CPI 1.02-1.06, food PPI 1.02-1.08, packaging 1.02-1.09, cost index 1.01-1.02. Best of 200 x lags 5-7 chosen in real time: 1.013-1.029. Without the episode SE food PPI reaches 0.92-0.96 (CW p 0.02-0.04), but without episode+echo the ratios are 0.95-1.07.
verdicts.residual_doubt: A delayed price catch-up is economically plausible, and the dairy and bakery signal keeps t of about 2.8-3.4 outside both cycles. With only 2-3 cost cycles, a weak genuine lead cannot be ruled out.

verdicts.corrected_statement: 4Q changes in 10y yields correlate negatively with d_margin: -0.99pp per +1pp (Norway, t -4.9) and -0.93pp (Orkla-weighted, t -5.1). This survives placebo calibration, block bootstrap, dropping 2021Q3-23Q4 (t -3.0 to -3.5) and a packaging-cost control (t -3.2 to -3.8), but it relies on the 2007 and 2022 cost-shock quarters: dropping episode, COVID and break quarters gives b=-0.38 and t of -1.9 to -2.4. It is the best single OOS predictor ex post in the full sample (RMSE ratio 0.93/0.90/0.92 at h0-2). Without the episode the ratio is 1.007-1.013 at h0 and 0.96-1.00 at h1-2, so it has no OOS value outside the episode.
verdicts.evidence: Orkla-weighted: placebo 95% |t| 2.34 (p<0.001); circular-shift p 0.011; bootstrap CI [-1.31,-0.50]. Without the episode: t -3.0, placebo p 0.010. Without episode+COVID: t -2.8, p 0.018. Before 2020: t -3.0. Norway without the episode: t -3.5, placebo p 0.002. Controls: packaging -> t -3.2 full, -3.0 without the episode; plastics -3.4 / -3.0; food PPI -3.4 / -3.0; raw materials -4.5 / -3.0. Without episode+COVID+breaks: Orkla-weighted -0.38 (t -1.9), Norway -0.39 (t -2.4). Covariance share of the episode is only 37%. OOS h0 (Norway): full 0.931 (CW 0.048); without the episode 1.013; without COVID+episode 1.053; 2015+ 0.878. h1: 0.901 full, 0.997 without the episode.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Calling yields a proxy for the inflation and cost cycle is an interpretation: in sample the relation survives the cost controls I tried, so a genuine rates or financing channel is not excluded.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Simple regressions show no same-quarter EUR/SEK effect on d_margin: -0.16pp per 10% at lag 0 (t -0.6) and +0.13pp at lag 1. The 'best real-time nowcast' result exists only against the weak AR(1)+Easter benchmark (RMSE ratio 0.986 full, 0.969 without the episode). Against the standard AR(1,4) with COVID quarters excluded from training, the EUR/SEK PDL adds nothing (0.993-1.007), and the plain AR(1,4) beats the EUR/SEK-augmented AR(1)+Easter model without the episode (RMSE 0.939 vs 0.975). The text fact holds: management cites weak FX in 25 quarters, when EUR/SEK y/y is +5.6% vs -0.5% otherwise.
verdicts.evidence: In-sample per 10%: lag 0 -0.16 (t -0.63; placebo p 0.60); lag 1 +0.13 (t 0.67); lag 2 +0.51 (t 2.4, p_cal 0.043, wrong sign for the claim); sum of lags 0+1 -0.01. OOS, mechanism set-up (AR1+Easter, COVID in training, min_train 28): ratio 0.986 (R2 +0.028, CW p 0.041) full, 0.969 (R2 +0.060, CW p 0.009) without the episode, 1.003 for 2015+. The lens reported R2 +0.06/+0.09 and p 0.011/0.002, so I get smaller gains. Against AR(1,4): PDL 1.007 / 1.006 (CW 0.13 / 0.07), lag 0 only 1.014, lags 0+1 1.024. Benchmark RMSEs (full / without episode): AR1+Easter 1.072 / 1.006; AR1 1.060 / 0.997; AR(1,4) 1.059 / 0.939. Text theme fx_weak: 25 quarters, EUR/SEK y/y +5.57% vs -0.48%.
verdicts.residual_doubt: A lagged SEK pass-through might show up in a richer specification with commodity controls (the mechanism lens reported -0.82pp at lag 1 controlling for USD commodities). Plain univariate and OOS evidence does not support it.

verdicts.corrected_statement: From 2010, no macro model robustly beats the d_margin AR(y_{t-h-1}, y_{t-4}). Over about 200 core features x h0-2 x 4 evaluation samples, 0 univariate models pass BY<0.10. The best gains are 4-7% RMSE: input-cost theory model at h0 0.953 (fails at h1/h2 with 1.002/1.102), first principal component 0.952/0.969/0.934, plastics PPI 0.947/0.913, packaging 0.965. Real wages, confidence, policy-rate and yield levels, nominal wages and energy have no robust in-sample margin effect after placebo calibration.
verdicts.evidence: Univariate OOS: best full-sample ratios are 0.931 (h0), 0.901 (h1) and 0.905-0.92 (h2), and 31-41% of models have a ratio below 1; BY<0.1 in every cell is 0. Theory model h0: CW 0.031 full, 0.006 without the episode (ratio 0.962). PCA1 without the episode: 0.967/0.981/0.983. Null variables at coincident, h0 and h1: real wages |t|<=1.6 full (calibrated p>=0.14); confidence |t|<=0.4 full; policy-rate level |t|<=0.3; 10y yield level |t|<=0.8; wage growth |t|<=0.8 (acceleration -1.9, p 0.09); energy full -1.8 to -3.1 (gas h1 p_cal 0.022) but without the episode |t|<=1.4. Without the episode a few wrong-signed hits appear (confidence z t -2.5 to -2.9, p_cal 0.01-0.03; real wage h1 t -2.6), and these would not survive multiplicity.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Margins are idiosyncratic (M&A, ERP and Easter noise), so a modest macro signal may exist but cannot be detected in 66 evaluation quarters.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Organic growth rises about 0.55-0.6pp per 1pp of Orkla-weighted food CPI ex VAT in the full sample (t 8.5; block-bootstrap t 4.4, CI 0.38-0.90), but the elasticity is not stable. By era it is 0.52 (2001-07), 1.03 (2008-14Q3), about 0 to -0.8 (2013-20 / 2014Q4-19) and 0.48 (2022-26); equality is rejected at p=0.003. Without the episode it is 0.60 (WLS t 2.6, placebo p 0.06; OLS t 3.5, p 0.01). The price-component fit for 2022Q2-26Q2 (slope 0.97, R2 0.85) is real but is one cycle: residual autocorrelation is 0.68, the first-difference slope is 0.77 (t 4.2), and the block-bootstrap slope CI is 0.01-1.24.
verdicts.evidence: Full sample: WLS 0.554 (t 8.5; HAC8 8.3), OLS 0.584 (8.6); placebo 95% |t| 2.59; circular-shift p 0.011. Without the episode: WLS 0.599, t 2.58, placebo 95% |t| 2.68, p_cal 0.059, bootstrap t 2.16 (CI 0.07-1.20); OLS 0.672, t 3.51, p_cal 0.012. Without breaks 0.84 (t 3.3); before 2020 0.73 (t 3.3). By era (WLS): 2001-07 0.52 (2.2), 2008-14Q3 1.03 (5.0), 2014Q4-19 -0.81 (-2.1, sd of x only 0.54), 2013-20 0.05 (0.07), 2022-26 0.475 (7.2). Wald test across 3 eras: chi2 14.1, p 0.003. The episode supplies 70% of the covariance. Price component, n=17: -0.233 + 0.971x, R2 0.853, exact OLS t 9.3 (invalid: residual rho1 0.68, DW 0.64). Slope=1 is not rejected (t -0.28). Slope in differences 0.765 (t 4.2, n=16). Q2-only (n=5): slope 1.16, r 0.95. Leave-one-year-out slope 0.88-1.05. Block bootstrap (block 4): CI [0.01, 1.24]. Nordic CPI: slope 1.27 (R2 0.91) rejects slope=1 (t 2.6); first difference 0.92 (t 5.3). PPI lag (Orkla-weighted): R2 at lag 0 / 1 / 2 = 0.69 / 0.90 / 0.82; lag 1 beats lag 0 in 95% of block-bootstrap draws (CI of the R2 difference 0.002-0.46). Nordic: 0.75 / 0.92 / 0.78 (94.5%).
verdicts.residual_doubt: The low-inflation eras have too little food-CPI variation (sd about 0.5pp) to pin the elasticity down. Definition noise (India, distribution deals 2015-16) may explain the negative 2014Q4-19 slope.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Selling-price expectation levels lead og by 1-2 quarters in the full sample (Swedish retail t 9.0, SSB t 6.0, EC food industry t 5.7; all placebo p<0.01), but only marginally without the episode (t 2.4-3.2, placebo p 0.03-0.15). The headline euro-area C10 d4 -> d_og h=4 result (t 5.2) is a base effect: controlling the base og_{t-4} cuts it to t 2.7 full and 0.95 without the episode, and against og itself it is t 2.2 (p_cal 0.08). OOS on the og AR base the full-sample gains are 1-11%, but without the episode the ratios are 0.94-1.06; only SSB d4 at h2 keeps a gain (0.943, CW p 0.006).
verdicts.evidence: ea_ec_food_ind_sell_price_exp__d4 -> d_og: h4 t 5.16 (HAC8 5.28; p_cal 1e-4), without the episode 4.69. With the og_{t-4} control: 2.73 full / 0.95 without the episode. h2: 5.86 -> with the control 1.97 / 0.13. Against og: h1 0.6, h2 1.2, h4 2.17 (without the episode 1.1). Survey levels -> og: SE retail h1 8.96 (without episode 3.04, p_cal 0.034; with food-CPI control 3.6); SSB level h2 5.96 (without episode 2.74, p_cal 0.054); Orkla-weighted EC food-industry level h2 5.68 (without episode 2.42, p_cal 0.078); SSB d4 h4 4.53 (without episode 2.74, p_cal 0.027). OOS og (AR og_{t-h-1}, og_{t-4}; full / without episode): SE retail 0.893 / 0.982 (h1), 0.887 / 0.979 (h2); SSB d4 h2 0.897 / 0.943; SSB level h2 0.901 / 1.011; EC food-industry level 0.966 / 1.021 (h1); ea d4 h2 0.954 / 1.014.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Survey levels do carry some information without the episode (t about 2.5-3). With roughly 20 survey variants x 3 horizons x 2 targets searched, the survivors may be selected.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Real-wage growth and confidence are negatively related to og (full t -5 to -7.6), with no positive volume effect; without the episode the volume-proxy slope on real wages is negative. The negative partial correlation partly survives a food-CPI control (real wage at h0, without the episode, t -2.6 to -3.7), so 'inflation mirror' is only part of the story. Granger causality runs both ways for Nordic confidence (og -> confidence p<1e-4; confidence -> og p 0.002-0.012). The Nordic nowcast reproduces (RMSE -5.7%, CW p 0.004), but its gain comes from real wage and confidence: the food-CPI term adds nothing, and dropping it improves the ratio to 0.922.
verdicts.evidence: og on Orkla-weighted / Nordic real wage: coincident t -5.2 / -4.0, h0 -7.6 / -6.0 (placebo p<=0.002). Without the episode: coincident -1.0 / -1.6, h0 -2.3 / -3.5. With food-CPI control at h0 without the episode: -2.6 / -3.7. Volume proxy on real wage: full +0.19 (t 0.6), without the episode -0.65 (t -2.7). Confidence (Orkla-weighted / Nordic): full -2.08 (t -5.6) / -1.99 (t -7.2); without the episode -2.4 / -3.2; with CPI control full -2.1 / -3.0, without the episode -1.7 / -2.7. Granger, 4 lags, HAC: og -> confidence p<1e-4 in all 4 specifications; confidence -> og p 0.012 (Nordic), 0.002 (Nordic, without COVID), 0.079 (Orkla-weighted), 0.018 (Orkla-weighted, without COVID). Nowcast ratio: 0.943 full (CW 0.004), 0.922 without the episode (0.011), 0.965 without COVID+episode (0.043), 0.928 2015+. Without food CPI: 0.922 (CW 0.002). Single variables: real wage 0.945, confidence 0.953, food CPI 1.014.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Granger tests on overlapping y/y data over-reject. A confidence -> og p of 0.01 may not survive an honest critical value, so the direction question stays open.

verdicts.corrected_statement: The volume proxy tracks Orkla's reported volume/mix (r=0.83, n=17, block-bootstrap CI 0.40-0.93) and is unpredictable in real time (0 of 195 features pass calibrated BY at h1 or h2). Its relative-food-inflation slope (-0.90 full, t -4.4) shrinks to -0.48 without the episode (t -1.8, placebo p 0.19), and it cannot be separated from incomplete price pass-through: with a food-CPI control it is t -1.7. Same-quarter co-movement with real disposable income and GDP is not significant after placebo calibration (p 0.06 / 0.14) and is zero without the episode. Unemployment at h2 improves og forecasts without the episode (RMSE ratio 0.949, DM p 0.003), but not in the full sample (DM p 0.22). Its in-sample t is only -2.4, and it does not predict the volume proxy.
verdicts.evidence: Proxy r=0.826, 0.895 excluding 2025. Relative food inflation: full -0.898 (t -4.36; placebo 95% |t| 2.55, p 0.001); without the episode -0.48 (t -1.76, p_cal 0.19); without episode+COVID -0.53 (t -1.7); before 2020 -0.33 (t -1.0); the episode supplies 70% of the covariance. With the food-CPI level as a control: full -0.79 (t -1.7), without the episode -0.43 (t -0.8). Real income: +1.03 (t 2.6, p_cal 0.057); without the episode +0.24 (t 0.7). GDP: +0.32 (t 2.0, p_cal 0.14); without the episode +0.17 (t 1.3). Real-time scan: best |t| 3.9-4.1 (p_cal 0.003-0.004) with BY 1.0. Unemployment w_unemp_d4 at h2 for og: full 0.968 (CW 0.026, DM t 0.76, p 0.22); without the episode 0.949 (CW t 5.4, p 4e-8, inflated by the CW adjustment term, mean 0.77 vs an MSE gain of 1.03; DM t 2.7, p 0.003). h1: 0.995-1.003. In sample og at h2: t -2.4 full, -2.5 without the episode. Volume proxy at h2: +0.66 full, -1.1 without the episode.
verdicts.residual_doubt: The proxy assumes price pass-through of 1 and fails in 2025. The unemployment result came from choosing the evaluation sample without the episode after seeing the results, so DM p=0.003 would not survive the roughly 5,000-test global family.

verdicts.corrected_statement: corr(d_og_t, og_{t-4}) = -0.64 is pure arithmetic: with og's lag-4 autocorrelation of 0.16 the identity implies -0.65. The og-level AR's OOS R2 vs a zero forecast (0.49 / 0.47 / 0.40) mostly reflects knowing og_{t-4}; against the prevailing mean, og's own AR has R2 0.25 / 0.24 / 0.14. Food CPI and PPI acceleration explains d_og in the same quarter (+0.24 to +0.33pp per 1pp; placebo p<=0.017), but without the episode this works entirely through the base: with og_{t-4} controlled the coefficient is 0.02-0.07 (t 0.1-0.4), against t 2.1-3.1 in the full sample.
verdicts.evidence: n=98: correlation -0.643, og acf at lag 1 / 2 / 4 = 0.51 / 0.49 / 0.16; implied value -sqrt((1-0.163)/2) = -0.647. og-level AR for d_og, R2 vs zero: 0.485 / 0.470 / 0.404 at h0 / 1 / 2 (without the episode 0.50 / 0.59 / 0.51). og AR vs prevailing mean: ratio 0.866 / 0.871 / 0.928. Food-CPI acceleration (coincident): 0.33 (t 4.7, p_cal 0.001), without the episode 0.44 (t 4.7); at h0 0.24 (t 3.5, p_cal 0.017). Food-PPI acceleration at h0: Nordic 0.32 (t 4.5), Orkla-weighted 0.28 (t 4.9); without the episode 0.35-0.43 (t 5.6). With og_{t-4} controlled: full 0.22-0.31 (t 2.1-3.1); without the episode 0.015-0.067 (t 0.10-0.43). Without breaks the coefficients are 0.40-0.55 (t 3.4-5.3).
verdicts.residual_doubt: The og_{t-4} control is itself correlated with food inflation four quarters earlier (pi_{t-4}), so the split between 'base' and 'acceleration' is not fully identified.

verdicts.corrected_statement: 4Q changes in Orkla-weighted policy rates lead og positively by 2-4 quarters in sample: +1.0 to +1.2pp per 1pp, t 3.5-4.3, placebo p 0.001-0.008, and t 2.7-3.7 without the episode. The relation comes from 2001-12 and 2022-23: it is insignificant in 2013-20 (t 0.6-1.5) and at h4 in 2013-26 (t 0.9). Out of sample it adds 4% RMSE at h2 in the full sample (CW 0.038) and nothing without the episode (0.988, p 0.11). It is a nominal-cycle proxy with low confidence.
verdicts.evidence: h2: 1.13 (t 3.83; HAC8 4.26; placebo 95% |t| 2.55, p 0.003); without the episode 0.75 (2.68); without episode+COVID 0.68 (2.46); before 2020 0.74 (2.2). h3: 1.17 (4.25), without the episode 0.96 (3.71). h4: 1.04 (3.48), without the episode 0.93 (3.69), before 2020 1.23 (7.0). Eras: 2001-12 t 2.3 / 4.6 / 7.0; 2013-26 2.8 / 1.9 / 0.9; 2013-20 0.6 / 1.1 / 1.5 (h2 / h3 / h4). Real-time food-CPI control at h2: t 3.1; own og_{t-h-1} control: 3.1. OOS og: h1 0.984 full / 1.002 without the episode; h2 0.959 / 0.988.
verdicts.residual_doubt: This is essentially two episodes (2007-08 and 2022-23) in which hikes preceded price-driven og surges, so it is unlikely to generalise.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Over-rejection is real but somewhat smaller than claimed. In my own matched AR(2) placebos the median nominal 5% HAC(4) size is 9-13%, with 95% |t| thresholds of 2.25-2.56 for random core features, a median of 2.45-2.68 by target across all core features at h0, and 2.5-2.9 for the persistent or spiky headline features. HAC(8) does not fix it. The 2021Q3-23Q4 share of the evidence depends on the target: 70% of the covariance for packaging -> d_margin, food CPI -> og and relative food -> volume, but 33-37% for yields -> d_margin and food-CPI acceleration -> d_og. The median t without the episode as a share of the full t is 0.71 (d_margin), 0.76 (d_og), 0.40 (og) and 0.31 (volume proxy). For lag-5-7 results the correct exclusion must also drop the 2022Q4-25Q3 echo.
verdicts.evidence: g1_placebo_size.csv: 60 random core features x 3 targets, 500 draws each. Median size and 95% |t|: d_margin 9.2% / 2.25 (HAC4), 9.3% / 2.27 (HAC8); og 12.8% / 2.51; d_og 12.0% / 2.56 (HAC8 12.8% / 2.65). By persistence: AR1>0.8 gives size 11-12% and 95% |t| about 2.45-2.5. Lag-scan h0, all core features: median 95% |t| 2.45 (d_margin), 2.46 (og), 2.55 (d_og), 2.68 (volume proxy); 90th percentile 2.63-2.88. Headline features: packaging 2.74 (size 17%), food CPI -> og 2.59, without the episode 2.68, food-PPI acceleration -> d_og 2.90. Covariance shares of the 10 episode quarters: packaging 0.70, NO yields 0.37, food CPI -> og 0.70, food-CPI acceleration -> d_og 0.33, relative food -> volume 0.70, raw materials 0.53. Rows with |t|>2 that keep their sign and |t|>1.645 without the episode: d_margin 66%, d_og 67%, og 37%, volume proxy 25%.
verdicts.residual_doubt: Gaussian AR(2) placebos do not reproduce one-off spikes like 2022, which inflate HAC t further. Circular-shift and block-bootstrap t were often about half the HAC t (packaging -9.6 vs -4.8), so honest thresholds for spike-driven regressors may be above 3.

new_findings: Echo contamination: for lagged (k=5-7) d_margin results, the lenses' sample without 2021Q3-23Q4 is not independent of the episode. Quarters 2022Q4-25Q3, whose lag-5-7 regressors are episode values, supply 42% of cov(d_margin, EU dairy PPI k=6), and 2024Q2-Q3 alone 29%. Dropping them takes the lag-scan t-stats from 4.2-5.2 down to 2.7-3.4 (dairy, bakery, SE food PPI, SE CPI) and 1.2-1.4 (weighted food PPI, packaging). Any 'robust without the episode' claim about lagged regressors should also drop the echo window.

With placebo calibration, the M3 lag-scan headline (dairy PPI k=6, nominal BY q 0.004) becomes BY q 0.24 within the 1,400-test d_margin family, Bonferroni 1 over 8,400. Circular-shift two-sided p is only 0.02-0.06. No positive-sign k>=4 d_margin row passes calibrated BY<0.10.

Survey -> d_og leads are base effects. Controlling the exact base og_{t-4}, rather than og_{t-5} as the screen did, cuts ea_ec_food_ind_sell_price_exp__d4 from t 5.2 to 2.7 at h4 and from 5.9 to 2.0 at h2; without the episode the values are 0.95 and 0.13.
Food CPI/PPI acceleration -> d_og without the episode also works entirely through the base: with og_{t-4} controlled, t is 0.1-0.4.

M5's EUR/SEK OOS gain is a benchmark artefact. The mechanism lens's AR(1)+Easter benchmark has RMSE 1.006 without the episode, against 0.939 for AR(1,4) with COVID excluded from training. Against AR(1,4), EUR/SEK gives ratio 1.006-1.007.
Nordic og nowcast: the food-CPI ex VAT term adds nothing out of sample. Dropping it improves the RMSE ratio from 0.943 to 0.922 (CW 0.002); the gain comes from real wages and confidence.
Clark-West can badly overstate OOS significance. For w_unemp_d4 (og, h2) without the episode, CW t is 5.4 (p 4e-8) while the Diebold-Mariano t is 2.7 (p 0.003). In the full sample, DM p is 0.22.

The 10y-yield d_margin relation in sample depends on the 2007 and 2022 cost-shock quarters. Dropping episode, COVID and definition-break quarters (incl. 2007Q2-Q4) halves the coefficient to -0.38 and gives t of -1.9 to -2.4.
Packaging: block-bootstrap t (-4.8) is half the HAC t (-9.6), and before 2020 t is -1.9. Without the episode, no core feature survives BY for d_margin at h0: packaging ranks 11th and plastics 17th.

The O1 price-component regression (n=17) cannot support its stated p-values. Residual AR(1) is 0.68 and DW 0.64, so with an effective sample of about 2 cycle observations the reported p<1e-6 is not meaningful. Defensible evidence is the first-difference slope of 0.77 (t 4.2) and a block-bootstrap slope CI of [0.01, 1.24].
corr(d_og, og_{t-4}) = -0.643 equals the arithmetic value of -0.647 implied by og's lag-4 autocorrelation of 0.16, so it carries no structural information.

Raw-material distributed-lag recovery: in the full sample the margin-level response does not reach half recovery within 12 quarters, and 56% of bootstrap draws never recover. The 6-7 quarter recovery comes only from the estimate without the episode, whose trough is not significant (t -1.7). The trough lag also depends on the specification: lag 0 unrestricted, 2-3 with a PDL.
